sections.title: A neighbourhood named after a Roman bath
paragraphs: Rómaifürdő is a residential neighbourhood of District III. Its name recalls a bathhouse of the second century that supplied water to Aquincum. The area around the springs was venerated as a holy place, and archaeologists have found the foundations of a sanctuary within the bath area as well as traces of spring-capturing structures. On 12 December 2012 the city assembly redrew the boundary so that all archaeological and listed monument areas of the Roman city belong to the Aquincum neighbourhood instead.

sections.title: Mills, a hospital and the bathing years
paragraphs: Later history is thinner but traceable. Under King Matthias a hospital was founded beside a lake here, and in the fifteenth century the local water powered gunpowder mills. From 1873 the area was known as Lőpormalomdűlő, the gunpowder-mill hollow. Bathing grew in the early twentieth century, and the Római strand opened as a public bath in 1965. The bath stands on Rozgonyi Piroska utca and operates as a seasonal summer bath rather than all year, so its current season is worth confirming with the operator.

sections.title: The Pók utca estate
paragraphs: A second layer is the Pók utca housing estate, also called the Római lakótelep, built between 1984 and 1989 south of Monostori út, mostly on land that had been farmland and allotments. It has 4,390 flats and roughly 12,400 residents, which makes everyday Rómaifürdő a place of tower blocks, school runs and shops more than of sightseeing. The Danube-side part of the neighbourhood is the southern end of the Római-part promenade, treated under its own page.

sections.title: Position
paragraphs: On the Szentendre suburban line the stops run Aquincum, Rómaifürdő, Csillaghegy and Békásmegyer, so the neighbourhood sits between the Roman city and the northern housing districts of Óbuda-Békásmegyer. The Rómaifürdő stop lies a short walk from the bath, and the Roman city is displayed at the Aquincum stop. Pünkösdfürdő nearby has a beach and a park that opened in 2022. The suburban line starts at Batthyány tér, which makes the neighbourhood an easy outing from central Buda, although it is a long way from the Castle District or the inner city.
